testcase.name: queued old generation send cannot write to a rapid reconnection
firmware maximum can be smaller than ATT capability
pipelining is independent firmware opt in not inferred from MTU
verified write commands skip acknowledged write pacing as in the source
without response capability requires characteristic and verified firmware evidence
concurrent writes are serialized through completion not just initial calls
cancelling a queued send does not cancel the unrelated active write
write pacing applies to sequential and queued acknowledged writes
write only ESP32 characteristic stays on acknowledged writes
MTU minus three and the firmware limit both constrain complete writes
unverified without response falls back to acknowledged send
larger unverified firmware frames fail before issuing or truncating
write commands and acknowledged writes share the entire operation queue
ATT attribute maximum is 512 and oversized commands are never split
write readiness timeout is exactly five seconds and invalidates its GATT
firmware capabilities cannot be replaced or inherited by a new generation
stale write callback is dropped instead of resuming the newer write
